questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was a city I've always really loved and I've known I've always wanted to move there. Nothing else.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. Uni Wien has a welcome day for all erasmus students where they give you all the relevant information + you can find lot's of information online on their website, on moodle and on uspace.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction class for erasmus students + information online + mails they would send out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy. Wihast is very big and popular among students, they have a lot of different places.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: if you want to live alone + own bathroom you might have to live a bit further away from the city centre

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Introduction class (to prove you had started) where you got your enrolment letter and student ID. Registration to classes was all online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Introduction class and a lot of information could be found online on their students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful, I got the ones I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for more (more ECTS) because most likely there will be some that you dont get or there will be overlaps in your schedule

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were nice and there was a big variety, however they were not very challenging compared to back home. The assessment was also very strange and it sometimes it felt like you could easily do nothing all semester and still get a good grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not as much active participation from the students. There is more focus on the teacher and a complete lack of exercises during the class, meaning it is more just learning theory, but you don't actually learn how to use it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Mostly just as I had expected it, which was cheaper than back home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were specifically a lot of sport options, which I know many erasmus students have used. Otherwise not that many activities from the Uni, more from ESN.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports - I've heard it was good, didn't personally join any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the citys location by see neighbouring cities and countries. Vienna is very central in Europe so there are many good options for taking weekend trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, personally I found them to be quite similar to copenhageners, so it was not hard.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I dont have any tips because we did not socialise with them. Uni Wien and ESN does nothing to help this, so if you want to befriend local students you have to really put and effort in yourself and be extroverted and perhaps look for local friends other places than in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Kept forgetting that supermarkets closed on sundays, different from back home. Otherwise none.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Christmas culture is very big (all the christmas markets). Good food and good beer.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Say yes to all social things (especially ESN in the beginning, good way to meet people)
2. Travel to other cities and countries close to Vienna
3. Use the city and don't just sit at home - do stuff on your own in the city too.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No there is not.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: For sure the friends you make from different countries and the experiences you now share together. Also becoming more independent and living on your own in a different country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did not really face any big challenges personally, but perhaps not seeing family and friends from back home all the time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
